subject: Build a multidimensional score card / composite indicator to measure a latent variable through SEM

messages.author: 79651afce853d690
messages.subject: Build a multidimensional score card / composite indicator to measure a latent variable through SEM
parts:
Hi,

I am thinking of using SEM - specifically with MIMIC model on a household survey to build a multidimensional score/index that will bring together both formative and reflective indicators (inspired by the FAO Resilience Index Measurement and Analysis)

The idea is to classify a population according to the resulting score on a latent variable (in my case vulnerability). The model would be calibrated on a representative sample. Once the composite indicator defined (i.e. list of observed indicators with respective weight), the resulting composite indicator could be then calculated for any new member of my population that will be monitored afterward.


The latent variable that should be measured through the composite indicators is the vulnerability. The model is likely to look like:


model.vulnerability <- '
    risk <~ household.size + dependency + asset + shelter + occupation + access.assistance + specific.need + purchase.power
    coping <~ access.education + access.health + access.credit + access.job + negative.mechanism
    vulnerability =~ access.documentation + denial.right + inclusion.community + exposure.violence
    risk + coping =~ vulnerability'


Once the model is fit and assessed through CFA, how can I extract the weight to be used for each observed indicators in order to calculate the vulnerability scorecard?


I looked at lavPredict(fit) and lavScores(fit) but it does not extract weights for indicators...


Sorry for my dummy question if it appears so...


Thanks,

Edouard

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Build a multidimensional score card / composite indicator to measure a latent variable through SEM
parts: I looked at lavPredict(fit) and lavScores(fit) but it does not extract weights for indicators...

Reading the descriptions on the help page of each function will tell you what these functions provide, neither of which are what you seem to want. You are looking for the regression weights?  There are many ways to get them, in vector or matrix format, or with SEs and test statistics:

inspect(fit, "est")
coef(fit)
parameterEstimates(fit)
